costNodePlain: Money set aside for loans that may not be repaid — the provision for credit losses: $2,231M of loans were charged off in the quarter and an $821M net reserve build was added, mostly in Consumer, primarily Card Services.

opex.name: Compensation expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost, up 15% YoY on employee growth and higher revenue-related compensation.

opex.name: Professional & outside services
opex.note: Professional fees and outside services, as reported in the supplement — up 6% YoY.

opex.name: Technology, communications & equipment
opex.note: Technology, communications and equipment — up 8% YoY as the bank invests in its platforms.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and card marketing — up 9% YoY.

opex.name: Occupancy & other expense
opex.note: Branches and offices ($1,248M of occupancy) plus other expense ($3,122M) — that other-expense line includes the $1.0B donation of Visa shares to the Firm's Foundation and $317M of legal expense.

follow100Note: JPMorgan reports revenue two ways: $50.2B reported (GAAP), used here, or $51.0B on a 'managed' basis that grosses up tax-exempt income by $792M ($115M of net interest income and $677M of noninterest revenue). Net income is identical either way. The rows reconcile to the $100 total within a cent of rounding.
footerNote: JPMorgan headlines 'managed' revenue of $51.0B; this page uses reported (GAAP) revenue of $50.2B — the $792M difference is a fully taxable-equivalent gross-up of tax-exempt income ($115M in net interest income and $677M in noninterest revenue) that does not change net income. For a bank, credit costs (the provision for credit losses) play the role of cost of revenue, and 'operating profit' here is income before income taxes.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: reported basis, vs a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $4.75 a year ago — $4.40 excluding significant items

oneTimers: $7.9B net gain related to Visa shares — JPMorgan tendered its 37.2 million Visa Class B-1 shares into Visa's exchange offer, receiving a combination of Visa Class B-2 and Class C shares; the gain on the Class C shares, held at fair value, was recorded in other income within noninterest revenue in Corporate. The release states it increased EPS by $2.04.

$1.0B donation of Visa shares to pre-fund contributions to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation — recorded in other expense in Corporate (it sits inside the 'Occupancy & other expense' bucket on this page) and reduced EPS by $0.18.
$546M of net investment securities losses in Corporate — the third 'significant item' flagged in the release; it reduced EPS by $0.14.

Excluding all three significant items, net income was $13.1B, EPS was $4.40 and ROTCE was 20%, versus reported net income of $18.1B, EPS of $6.12 and ROTCE of 28% — a $5.0B after-tax, $1.72-per-share difference, per the release.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, up 4% as balance-sheet mix, higher rates, higher revolving Card balances and one extra month of First Republic income outweighed deposit margin compression.

segments.name: Noninterest revenue
segments.note: Fees, trading and asset-management income — up 41%, largely because it included the $7.9B gain on Visa shares in other income; investment banking fees rose 52% to $2,304M and asset management fees 14% to $4,302M.

takeaways.text: Exchanging its Visa Class B-1 shares added a $7.9B net gain in Corporate and $2.04 to EPS. Together with the related $1.0B Foundation donation and $546M of securities losses, the quarter's significant items added $5.0B after tax — excluding them, net income was $13.1B and ROTCE was 20%, not 28%.
takeaways.title: One Visa gain did the heavy lifting

takeaways.text: Investment banking fees rose 52% to $2.3B, asset management fees 14% to $4.3B, and Markets revenue rose 10% (Fixed Income +5%, Equity Markets +21%) — so the underlying quarter grew even without the Visa gain.
takeaways.title: The fee engine was strong too

takeaways.text: The provision was $3,052M, up 5% YoY: net charge-offs of $2,231M were up 58% YoY, predominantly driven by Card Services, plus an $821M net reserve build, mostly in Consumer.
takeaways.title: Credit costs are normalizing upward

verdict: JPMorgan reported $18.1B of profit on $50.2B of revenue, but the headline was flattered by a $7.9B one-off gain on its Visa B shares — excluding the quarter's significant items, net income was $13.1B ($4.40 per share).
